There are several ways to run MSTest tests depending on your needs. You can run tests from an IDE (for example, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, or JetBrains Rider), or from the command line, or from a CI service (such as GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps).

Historically, MSTest relied on [VSTest](https://github.com/microsoft/vstest) for running tests in all contexts but starting with version 3.2.0, MSTest has its own test runner. This new runner is more lightweight and faster than VSTest, and it's the recommended way to run MSTest tests.

## VSTest vs MTP

This article covers advanced configuration options for MSTest.Sdk. For basic setup and getting started, see [Get started with MSTest](unit-testing-mstest-getting-started).

MSTest.Sdk sets `EnableMSTestRunner` and `TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport` to true by default. For more information about dotnet test and its different modes, see [Testing with dotnet test](unit-testing-with-dotnet-test).

## Test utility helper libraries

If the project that uses MSTest.Sdk is intended to be a test utility helper library, and doesn't by itself contain any runnable tests, the project should have `<IsTestApplication>false</IsTestApplication>`.

*   [Microsoft.Testing.Platform profile](#microsofttestingplatform-profile)
*   [Enable or disable extensions](#enable-or-disable-extensions)

### Microsoft.Testing.Platform profile

The concept of _profiles_ allows you to select the default set of configurations and extensions that will be applied to your test project.

You can set the profile using the property `TestingExtensionsProfile` with one of the following three profiles:

*   `None` - No extensions are enabled.

    *   [Trx Report](microsoft-testing-platform-test-reports#visual-studio-test-reports-trx)

    *   [Crash Dump](microsoft-testing-platform-crash-hang-dumps#crash-dump)
    *   [Fakes](microsoft-testing-platform-fakes) (MSTest.Sdk 3.7.0+)
    *   [Hang Dump](microsoft-testing-platform-crash-hang-dumps#hang-dump)
    *   [Hot Reload](microsoft-testing-platform-hot-reload#hot-reload)
    *   [Retry](microsoft-testing-platform-retry#retry)
    *   [Trx Report](microsoft-testing-platform-test-reports#visual-studio-test-reports-trx)
    *   [AzureDevOpsReport](microsoft-testing-platform-test-reports#azure-devops-reports)

<Project Sdk="MSTest.Sdk/4.1.0">

    </PropertyGroup>

# Migration Plan: VSTest → Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP)

## Problem

5 MSTest test projects currently use VSTest via individual package references (`MSTest.TestFramework`, `MSTest.TestAdapter`, `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` all at 3.8.0/17.13.0). Azure DevOps CI uses `VSTest@3` task with TRX reporting and code coverage. Goal: migrate all projects to Microsoft.Testing.Platform using MSTest SDK.

## Approach

Use **MSTest.Sdk** (recommended by Microsoft) which enables MTP by default, bundles TRX + code coverage in its `Default` profile, and dramatically simplifies `.csproj` files. This is a 2-phase migration: project files first, then CI pipeline.

---

## Phase 1 — Project File Migration

### 1. Add `global.json` with MSTest.Sdk version

Create or update `global.json` at the solution root:

```json
{
  "msbuild-sdks": {
    "MSTest.Sdk": "3.8.0"
  }
}
```

> Using 3.8.0 to stay on the same MSTest version you already use. You can bump to 4.x later when ready for .NET 9/10 SDK support.

### 2. Convert each `.csproj` to MSTest.Sdk

For every test project, apply these changes:

**Before:**
```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="MSTest.TestFramework" Version="3.8.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="MSTest.TestAdapter" Version="3.8.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.13.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

**After:**
```xml
<Project Sdk="MSTest.Sdk/3.8.0">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

Key removals:
- `Sdk` attribute changes from `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` → `MSTest.Sdk/3.8.0` (or omit version if using `global.json`)
- Remove all 3 MSTest/TestSdk `PackageReference` entries (SDK provides them)
- Remove `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>` (SDK sets this)
- Remove `<OutputType>Exe</OutputType>` if present (SDK sets this)

### 3. Add `Directory.Build.props` (optional, recommended)

If you want solution-wide control, add at the solution root:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport>true</TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport>
    <TestingPlatformShowTestsFailure>true</TestingPlatformShowTestsFailure>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

> `TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport` ensures `dotnet test` works with MTP.  
> `TestingPlatformShowTestsFailure` shows per-test failure output on the console.

### 4. Source code changes

**None required.** All `[TestClass]`, `[TestMethod]`, `[TestCategory]`, `Assert.*` APIs, `[DataRow]`, `[DynamicData]`, lifecycle hooks (`[TestInitialize]`, etc.) work identically under MTP. The `using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;` namespace stays the same.

### 5. Validate locally

```bash
dotnet test --no-build   # after building
# or simply:
dotnet test
```

With MTP, each test project compiles to an executable. `dotnet test` still works because of `TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport`. You can also run directly:

```bash
dotnet run --project MyTests -- --list-tests
dotnet run --project MyTests -- --filter "TestCategory=Slow"
```

---

## Phase 2 — Azure DevOps Pipeline Migration

### 6. Replace `VSTest@3` with `DotNetCoreCLI@2` (test command)

MTP test projects are standalone executables; the VSTest task is no longer needed.

**Before:**
```yaml
- task: VSTest@3
  inputs:
    testSelector: 'testAssemblies'
    testAssemblyVer2: '**/*Tests.dll'
    searchFolder: '$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)'
    resultsFolder: '$(Agent.TempDirectory)/TestResults'
    codeCoverageEnabled: true
```

**After:**
```yaml
- task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
  displayName: 'Run Tests'
  inputs:
    command: 'test'
    projects: '**/*Tests.csproj'
    arguments: >-
      --configuration Release
      --no-build
      --logger trx
      --results-directory $(Agent.TempDirectory)/TestResults
      --collect "Code Coverage"
```

### 7. Publish TRX results

TRX reports are generated via the `--logger trx` flag (the `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.TrxReport` package is included in MSTest.Sdk's `Default` profile).

```yaml
- task: PublishTestResults@2
  displayName: 'Publish Test Results'
  condition: always()
  inputs:
    testResultsFormat: 'VSTest'   # TRX format = "VSTest" in this task
    testResultsFiles: '$(Agent.TempDirectory)/TestResults/**/*.trx'
    mergeTestResults: true
```

### 8. Publish code coverage

The `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` package (also in `Default` profile) generates `.coverage` files.

```yaml
- task: PublishCodeCoverageResults@2
  displayName: 'Publish Code Coverage'
  condition: always()
  inputs:
    summaryFileLocation: '$(Agent.TempDirectory)/TestResults/**/*.cobertura.xml'
```

If you want Cobertura format instead of `.coverage`, pass:
```
--collect "Code Coverage;Format=Cobertura"
```

### 9. Update any `--filter` syntax

Filter syntax is unchanged. Both VSTest and MTP use the same filter expressions:

```
--filter "TestCategory=Slow"
--filter "FullyQualifiedName~Calculator"
```

### 10. Update `.runsettings` references (if any)

If you use a `.runsettings` file, pass it via `--settings`:

```
arguments: '--settings test.runsettings'
```

Most MSTest runsettings entries are supported. See: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/testing/unit-testing-mstest-configure#runsettings

---

## Phase 3 — Validation & Rollout

### 11. Run full CI pipeline on a feature branch

- Verify all 5 projects build and produce executables
- Verify TRX results appear in Azure DevOps test tab
- Verify code coverage report publishes correctly
- Verify test filters still work as expected

### 12. Roll out incrementally (optional)

You can migrate one project at a time. MSTest.Sdk projects and legacy VSTest projects can coexist in the same solution. Use `<UseVSTest>true</UseVSTest>` in MSTest.Sdk projects if you need to temporarily revert a project.

### 13. Clean up

- Remove any leftover `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`, `MSTest.TestAdapter`, `MSTest.TestFramework` package references
- Remove the `VSTest@3` task from all pipeline YAML files
- Delete unused `.runsettings` entries that are no longer supported

---

## Notes & Considerations

- **No source code changes** — test attributes, assertions, and namespaces are identical
- **MSTest.Sdk `Default` profile** bundles TRX + Code Coverage — no extra packages needed
- **`AllMicrosoft` profile** adds crash/hang dumps, retry, hot reload, Azure DevOps native reporting if desired
- **Rollback path** — add `<UseVSTest>true</UseVSTest>` to any MSTest.Sdk project to revert to VSTest
- **Performance** — MTP is faster than VSTest (no `vstest.console` process overhead; each test project is a standalone exe)
- **Parallel execution** — MTP runs tests in parallel by default; fine-tune via `[Parallelize]` assembly attribute or runsettings
- **Visual Studio** — Test Explorer works with MTP projects in VS 2022 17.8+
